text:
maria: FYI support #5468 — customer reports signed callback failures after we enabled delegated-scope. They see intermittent \"invalid signature\" for ~10% of callbacks, seemingly concentrated around EU DST shifts. Escalating to eng.

samir: linking ticket and logs https://redwood.support/t/5468, customer sent stack traces, looks like two different failures: \"kid not found\" and \"token not yet valid (nbf)\".

ingrid: pasted smallest repro log: 
```
validate_jwt: signature verification failed, kid=eu-ytx-2026 not found in cached JWKS
validate_jwt: token rejected: nbf=2026-03-29T01:00:00Z current=2026-03-29T00:00:20Z
trace_id=trc_0a1b2c
```
Header from failing token: 
```
{"alg":"RS256","kid":"eu-ytx-2026"}
```
Cached JWKS for issuer shows kid list: `["eu-ytx-2025","eu-abc-001"]` — no match.

tj: quick repro I ran from my laptop (EU TZ) — curl of callback endpoint that mimics auth header: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <jwt-with-kid-eu-ytx-2026>\" \\
  -d '{"event":"order.created"}' https://hooks.example.com/redwood-callback
```
Response: 401 Unauthorized, body: `{\"error\":\"invalid_signature\"}`.

opsbot: jwks-cache:ttl=300s (global), last_refresh=2026-03-29T00:58:32Z.

maria: interestingly we purged the JWKS cache manually at 01:10 => failures stopped for ~8 minutes then resumed. Customer reports retries sometimes succeed. That smells like JWKS rotation + cache race where a newly minted kid exists upstream but our nodes are still using stale cache and don't fetch on miss.

samir: also note the nbf errors line up with DST forward shift in CET zone on 2026-03-29 01:00. Customer system seems to mint tokens with local clock +1h offset; iat/nbf are in UTC but consumer system sent tokens that become valid an hour later.

ingrid: proposed immediate mitigations:
- on kid-miss, attempt an immediate JWKS refresh from issuer and revalidate before rejecting. pseudo: 
```
if verify(token) fails and reason == \"kid_not_found\":
  refresh_jwks(issuer)
  retry verify(token)
```
- apply small leeway for iat/nbf checks (e.g., 120s) to account for clock skew and DST edgecases.

tj: will open a runtime PR to implement refresh-on-kid-miss + 120s default leeway, plus an opt-out flag for strict mode. I'll also add a short-circuit to avoid thundering herd fetches (singleflight). Planning to ship hotfix to Dedicated pools and roll to hosted API as a config push.

maria: customer-side workaround we suggested: retry callbacks on 401 for 60s with exponential backoff and send us failed callback headers so we can trace. They can't update system clock.

ingrid: monitoring/alerts: add metric `jwks.kid_miss` and `jwt.nbf_rejects` with tag issuer=... and alert if >5/min per cluster. Also log the token kid and trace_id (strip actual tokens) for correlation. Query example: `filter @message like /kid_not_found/ | stats count() by cluster, kid`

opsbot: created incident incident/2026-03-29-kwjwks with runbook link https://confluence.redwood/kwjwks-runbook.

tj: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pulls/789 — patch adds refresh-on-miss + singleflight + 2min leeway env REDWOOD_JWT_LEEWAY=120. I'll coordinate rollout with eng-sre. ETA 2h for canary.

maria: assigning to tj to track patch and to ingrid to add alerts. I'll update support ticket and tell customer the immediate workaround to retry for 60s and to forward any failed headers. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

samir: one more note — CS reported a billing notification failed earlier today due to same callback path; double-check invoices for the impacted window and re-send hooks if needed.

maria: noted, pinging finance/systems to verify no lost invoices.

ingrid: after the hotfix we should also add an integration test that simulates: (1) issuer rotates key (new kid) (2) node has stale JWKS and receives token with new kid => should trigger fetch and accept. I'll add to infra tests.

maria: cool. I'll close the slack loop once PR is live and customer confirms.
